action_summary: Round 16's next step -- path-reaching input synthesis for a changed site -- implemented at the honest minimal faithful scale, under the field's own name for it (directed greybox fuzzing: WAFLGO directs at commit change sites, AFLGo/ColorGo score by distance to target, Driller/QSYM pair mutation with concolic solving). Seeds are the literal calls the human's own test makes; the mutation grammar is byte insert/delete/replace, line duplication and seed splicing; feedback is the set of lines executed in the target file, gathered by one traced child per batch of 40; retention keeps novel line-shapes and improving input-distance; the distance is the quantity the changed block compares against, read off the artifact; the assertion is emitted only if the generated input is green on the fix and red on the reverted part. Three bugs in this instrument were found and fixed before any number was believed: aiming at the if-header instead of the guarded body (every input 'reached'), measuring distance between line numbers (constant, corpus froze, zero progress), and a receipt that stored only the last line of the assertion so the claim was not checkable from it. A part that only removes code is refused rather than searched. Result: 17 real fixes, 8 unpinned behavioural parts (round 16's denominator), 2 refused, 6 searched in 693 executions, 2 reached and pinned and verified -- certified share 0.714 -> 0.762 -- and the 4 failures all compare against structure rather than a quantity, which is exactly where the field's state of the art depends on a model's one pass. The bottleneck is therefore named by measurement: reachability reasoning.
